query: Racing the Gulls The gulls over the lake race couriers for fun. The fisherman says the jar's wind won't follow you until you've beaten them once, flat out, from the jetty to the far bank. Race them flat out You hit the far bank a beak ahead of the lead gull. The wind in the jar turns over once, like a cat settling. The gulls follow you home, offended. You clip a wave at full speed and skip across the lake like a stone. The gulls are delighted. You are wet to the bone. Fly your round steady You fly the round steady and deliver everything dry. The gulls lose interest. So does the jar.

results.excerpt:
The Fisherman Waves
The old fisherman in the reed beds has never waved at a courier. Today, seeing the jar strapped to your broom, he waves, and beckons you down. "That jar," he says. "I flew it once. Fastest year of my life."
